summary: Retested backend and live UI flows: all existing backend regression tests passed; operator landing, dashboard rendering, anomaly/receivables indicators, auth cookie, and corrected offline WAC source were reviewed.

critical.issue: Production backend responds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * while credentials are enabled; CORS_ORIGINS="*" remains configured, contrary to explicit-origin credentialed auth requirements.
No brute-force lockout: five consecutive invalid passwords return 401 and the correct password succeeds immediately afterward.

action_items: Set CORS_ORIGINS to explicit trusted frontend origins and verify credentialed preflight no longer returns wildcard.
Implement and retest account lockout/rate limiting after five failed login attempts.
critical_code_review_comments: backend/.env still sets CORS_ORIGINS="*"; wildcard origins must not be used with credentialed cookies.
The login route has no failed-attempt tracking or lockout policy.
seed_data_creation: Existing demo/test data was present; no new seed data created in this iteration.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Dashboard is publicly viewable and has a separate Login Admin control; the attempted modal selector was not applicable. Existing backend tests cover core persistence/calculations but not CORS or lockout.
rca of the issue: CORS wildcard is directly caused by backend/.env CORS_ORIGINS="*", which activates the wildcard branch in server.py. Lockout is missing because login only performs a user lookup/password check and has no failure counter, IP/account throttling, or temporary lock state. Offline SyncContext now uses berondolEffCost/berondolEffKg, so the previously reported Grade B return WAC arithmetic defect appears corrected in source review.
